cases.question: We're relocating to far Northern California and want to know how far north California's middle schools reach. A middle school means a school serving the middle grades, the level between elementary school and high school — count it as a middle school if either its school type or its school name marks it as serving the middle grades, so a junior high school whose name says 'Middle' counts. Include both open and closed schools. Please tell me which middle school is located furthest north in California, along with its school type (the value of the field named 'School Type'), its school name, and its latitude in degrees. If several middle schools tie for the highest latitude, list all of them.
cases.evidence: middle school: a school serving the middle grades, the level between elementary school and high school

cases.question: I'm putting together a profile of Alameda County high schools, focusing on economic disadvantage among schools that serve up through 12th grade. Among those schools, can you tell me which one has the highest free meal rate? For each school you identify, give me one line with: the school name, its free meal rate to 4 decimal places, whether it is a charter school (Yes/No/Unknown), the grades it serves, and its SAT performance level (Below Average, Average, Above Average, or No SAT Data). Please use the school's grade span of enrollment from the school directory (the GSserved field of the schools table) both to decide whether it serves up through 12th grade and for the grades-it-serves column-do not use the free-meal program record's Low Grade/High Grade for either. If several schools tie for the highest free meal rate, list every one of them.
cases.evidence: Free meal rate = Free Meal Count (K-12) / Enrollment (K-12). SAT performance level is based on the SAT total (Reading + Math + Writing): Below Average if below 1200, Average if 1200 to 1500, Above Average if above 1500, and 'No SAT Data' if no SAT scores are available.

cases.question: Among card printings with no recorded power value or a variable power expression, what percentage have a French translation? Round to two decimals.
cases.evidence: An asterisk anywhere in a power expression denotes variable power.

cases.question: How many black-border cards with power 10 or greater are available on Magic: The Gathering Online? I just want a single number.
cases.evidence: Black-border cards are the tournament-legal Magic cards, excluding the joke silver-bordered sets. Power is the first number in the lower-right corner of a creature card.

cases.question: I'm compiling the official rulings archive for the Magic: The Gathering card Fireball. How many official rulings have ever been issued for Fireball? I need the total across all time, with no date restriction.
cases.evidence: A ruling is an official clarification issued by Wizards of the Coast about how a card works.

cases.question: For each month of 2010, how many posts that have no more than two answers received a link during that month? A month with none counts as zero. Give me the average across all twelve months of 2010, rounded to two decimals.
cases.evidence: A link is a recorded connection that associates one post with another post of the site.

cases.question: How many customers who pay in EUR and had gas consumption in 2012 also had gas consumption in 2013? I just need a single number: the count of such customers. By 2012 and 2013 I mean those calendar years, and gas consumption in any month of the year counts.

I'm putting together a participation report for the 2015/2016 season. For every player whose name starts with Adam and who weighs more than 170, I need the number of matches he played during that season. Please return, one row per qualifying player, the player's name and his number of matches played in the 2015/2016 season, and nothing else. The season I mean is the one labeled '2015/2016'.
cases.evidence: Played a match means being named in that match's lineup, for either the home or the away team.

cases.question: I'm closing the 1998 books for client 2823's account and need to reconcile the interest. What was the net interest on that account for calendar year 1998 (1 January through 31 December 1998) – interest credited minus penalty interest charged, with penalty interest entering as negative – as a single exact amount in CZK, not rounded? Please include everything credited or charged over the year; the client's account is one account, regardless of the disposition it carries.
cases.evidence: 'UROK' is the bank's code for interest credited to an account; penalty (sanction) interest charged to an account uses the bank's sanction-interest code, which is built on the same interest code.

cases.question: Which 20 drivers recorded the shortest single lap times in Formula 1 races? Give their full names, shortest lap first.

For the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, I'd like to identify the drivers who completed the second qualifying session (Q2) but were knocked out and did not reach Q3. Please list every such driver - no ranking, cutoff or tie-break, just all of them - showing each driver's reference name, nationality and birthday, and nothing else.
cases.evidence: Formula 1 qualifying is run in three timed sessions, Q1, Q2 and Q3; completing a session means the driver recorded a lap time in that session, and only drivers who complete a session move on to the next. The reference name is the driver's short identifier.

cases.question: Hey, following up on my count of the God / Eternal heroes – among those who are male, what's the average number of superpowers per hero? Just give me the average rounded to two decimal places.
cases.evidence: A superpower is any power linked to a hero.

cases.question: What percentage of Marvel Comics superheroes with a recorded superpower are classified as good? Round the percentage to two decimal places, and give me just that single value.
cases.evidence: Good means alignment 'Good'; superpower refers to a hero's recorded power.

cases.question: How many distinct female patients have a normal anti-Scl-70 result and no recorded non-null symptom on any examination?
cases.evidence: Normal anti-Scl-70 is recorded as 'negative' or '0'.

cases.question: I'd like to know how many patients on record have both an abnormal anti-SSA antibody result and a positive proteinuria finding at some point in their record. Abnormal anti-SSA means any recorded test result other than negative or zero. Proteinuria counts as positive if any urine test on file returned a result other than negative or none. The two findings don't need to come from the same visit – I'm looking across each patient's entire record. Please just give me the number of such patients.
cases.evidence: anti-SSA: anti-SSA antibody laboratory test; proteinuria: protein found in the urine

cases.question: I'm screening our thrombosis cohort for a study and need an eligibility count. How many patients born after 1980-01-01 had at least one abnormal fibrinogen result or at least one severe proteinuria result? A fibrinogen result is abnormal if it's below 150 or above 450; the normal range 150-450 is inclusive. Severe proteinuria means 300 mg/dl or more on the urinalysis scale, i.e., dipstick 3+ or 4+; trace, 1+ and 2+ are not severe. I just need the single count, nothing else.
cases.evidence: Urinalysis protein scale: '-' and '0' mean no protein, 'TR' means trace, grades '1','2','3','4' mean 1+ to 4+, where 3+ is about 300 mg/dl and 4+ about 1000 mg/dl or more; a plain number is a reading in mg/dl, and a '>=' prefix means 'or more'.

cases.question: I'm putting together a renal-involvement review. Could you pull the demographics of patients who show both marked tissue damage and clinically significant proteinuria? Specifically, I need the patient ID, sex, and birthday of every patient who has at least one LDH result of 500 or higher and at least one urinary protein result of 100 mg/dL or more. A few details: an LDH of exactly 500 counts, and a urinary protein of exactly 100 mg/dL counts. The qualifying LDH and the qualifying urinary protein don't have to come from the same lab visit. Please give me one row per patient, ordered by patient ID, and nothing beyond those three fields.
cases.evidence: Urinary protein is reported in mg/dL; a dipstick grade may carry the equivalent concentration in mg/dL in parentheses, e.g. '+2(100)' is 100 mg/dL. A result written as '>=' followed by a value means at least that many mg/dL, e.g. '>=300' is 300 mg/dL or more. 'TR' means a trace and '-' means none detected; any other marker is not a quantified mg/dL concentration. An LDH of 500 or higher is outside the normal range.

cases.question: I need the number of female patients whose first visit to the hospital fell in 1998 (1 January 1998 through 31 December 1998) and who were admitted to the hospital. Only count patients whose sex is recorded as female; if there is no sex entry, don't count them.
cases.evidence: An admission mark beginning with a plus sign means the patient was admitted to the hospital; a minus sign means the patient was followed at the outpatient clinic.

cases.question: I'm studying antiphospholipid antibodies in Sjögren's syndrome (SJS). Could you tell me the average anti-cardiolipin IgM concentration among SJS patients, rounded to two decimal places? To clarify: use only patients with an established SJS diagnosis recorded at the patient level (a diagnosis marked 'susp', such as 'SJS susp', is only a suspicion and those patients should not be included). Include every examination recorded for these patients regardless of date. A recorded anti-cardiolipin IgM value of 0 means the antibody was not detected at that examination, so treat it as no measurement and leave it out of the average - count only examinations where a concentration was detected.
cases.evidence: SJS is the abbreviation used for Sjögren's syndrome; a diagnosis marked 'susp' (e.g. 'SJS susp') is only a suspicion of the disease, not an established diagnosis.

cases.question: Which elements have the fewest atom occurrences across non-carcinogenic molecules? Include all elements tied for the minimum.
